title: Our struggle with addressing in South Africa: Capturing public stakeholder perspectives
why: Q1: reports no authoritative national address register, unclear governance, rural/township/informal gaps, and fragmented use by postal, utility, billing and emergency services (Q2-Q4).

title: A holistic categorisation of address purposes as an analytical entry point to finding solutions for addressing governance in South Africa
why: Q1: finds addresses are being rolled out but stakeholder responsibility and governance remain unclear; sets out uses across government and economy (Q3, Q4).

title: AFRIGIS Address Database (Layer ID 8)
why: Q2: a live, queryable address database layer in service, published August 2024; provincial, not proof of one national register.

title: South Africa, Rural addressing
why: Q2: describes SAPO assigning and maintaining rural and informal-area addresses (over 70% assigned since 2003) used for postal, emergency, utility and billing services (Q3, Q4); undated page.

title: The postal delivery database
why: Q2: describes a live database of box and residential addresses used for delivery and targeting, with a route to register residential addresses (Q4); undated page.

title: Naming & Renaming of Streets and Public Places Policy
why: Q1: current municipal street naming and numbering policy, tied to emergency, banking, postal and billing services (Q4); local, not national.

title: Policy on Street Naming, Renaming & House Numbering
why: Q1: current municipal rules for street naming and house numbering, showing local implementation under way; not whole-country coverage.

title: City of Johannesburg streamlines processes with new spatial data portal
why: Q2: citywide spatial-data portal centralising municipal data; city-level infrastructure, not a national address register.
